summary:
Across the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space, dozens of historic NASA spacecraft rest in permanent silence after completing their pioneering missions. While their official records exist in technical catalogs like the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), the public rarely experiences the human stories, engineering triumphs, and physical fate of this hardware.

	RELIC-OS is an interactive 3D web platform developed by Team N94R00T that brings every official NASA Challenge #01 spacecraft group to life. Combining an interactive Three.js 3D Planetary Globe (for both The Moon and Mars), authenticated NSSDCA Mission Dossiers, a Web Audio API LastContact Telemetry Synthesizer, a 2026-2050 Space Weathering & Radiation Decay Simulator, and a Future Artemis/Mars Salvage Manifest, RELIC-OS transforms static NASA archives into a living museum and engineering tool for the next frontier of space exploration.
details:
RELIC-OS is an interactive 3D planetary heritage and telemetry archive built by Team N94R00T for the NASA Space Apps Challenge Kuala Lumpur 2026 (Challenge #01: Abandoned but not Forgotten).

What It Does & How It Works: RELIC-OS maps 13 verified NASA NSSDCA spacecraft hardware groups left behind across The Moon (4 groups, including Apollo 11/12/15/16/17 LM, LRV, ALSEP, and Surveyor) and Mars (9 groups, including Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity) onto an interactive 3D WebGL globe. Users can switch between Lunar and Martian orbital views, inspect real-time 3D landing coordinates and NSSDCA telemetry dossiers, trigger live NASA Image & Video Library and DONKI space-weather lookups (with offline-resilient fallbacks), synthesize acoustic reconstructions of final spacecraft transmissions via Web Audio API, run a 2026–2050 Environmental Wear & Degradation Simulator (modeling thermal cycling, micrometeoroid flux, cosmic radiation, and dust abrasion), and export structured JSON salvage/heritage manifests.

Benefits & Intended Impact: By transforming static archival catalogs into a tactile, spatial, and predictive experience, RELIC-OS raises public awareness of off-world aerospace heritage, supports STEM education, and demonstrates a framework for tracking and preserving historic lunar and Martian sites ahead of future Artemis and crewed Mars missions.

Tools, Languages & Software Used: Developed as a zero-install, browser-native ES Module web application using JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, Three.js (WebGL) for 3D planetary rendering, Web Audio API for procedural telemetry audio synthesis, Vite for bundling, GitHub for version control, and Vercel for live deployment.

Creativity & Factors Considered: Instead of a plain table or map, RELIC-OS combines orbital 3D pinpointing, dual visual themes (Mission Control & Archival Paper), physics-inspired long-term surface degradation modeling (2026–2050), and procedural audio telemetry. Our team prioritized accessibility (keyboard navigation, ARIA live regions), scientific accuracy using official NSSDCA IDs and landing coordinates, and offline resilience if external API rate limits occur.
